mainTopic: רבי's ruling about animals found slaughtered, the שחיטה of a חרש, שוטה, and קטן, whether שחיטה needs כוונה, and whether a קטן has legally meaningful מחשבה
overview: The גמרא first finishes explaining רבי's statement about the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי. Each sage agrees with the other in one case: everyone follows רבי יהודה for a trash heap in the marketplace, and everyone follows רבי חנינא for a trash heap in the house. Next, the גמרא goes back to the משנה about a חרש, שוטה, and קטן. From the words 'שמא יקלקלו' (lest they ruin, in the future), רבא learns that we do not give them animals to slaughter לכתחילה. The משנה adds that if others watched them, their שחיטה is כשרה. The גמרא asks who holds that שחיטה needs no כוונה. רבא answers that it is רבי נתן, based on a ברייתא about a thrown knife, and the one who taught that ברייתא ruled הלכה כרבי נתן. The גמרא explains how a thrown knife could move back and forth: it bounced off the wall and came back. Finally, רבי יוחנן asks whether a קטן's מחשבה counts, and רבי אמי objects that a משנה about shells hollowed out by children already settles it. That משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How each opinion 'appears correct' to the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי's statement: רבי חנינא agrees with רבי יהודה about a trash heap in the marketplace, and רבי יהודה agrees with רבי חנינא about the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי means: רבי יהודה's view seems right even to רבי חנינא when the animals were found in a trash heap in the marketplace. רבי חנינא only argued about a trash heap in the house, but about the marketplace he agrees. And רבי חנינא's view seems right to רבי יהודה (in the house case).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question about רבי's puzzling words by showing that each sage admits the other is right in one specific place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it sounded as if רבי was saying both sides are right, which is confusing. The answer is that the two sages do not argue about everything. In the marketplace trash heap they both follow רבי יהודה, and in the house they both follow רבי חנינא, so their real argument is narrower than it first looked.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא explains someone's words)
A trash heap or garbage pile

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא is limited. Both agree in the marketplace trash heap case, and both agree in the house case.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, whose puzzling statement the גמרא was trying to understand just before this.

phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda appear correct

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: to Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
in the case of a trash heap that is in the marketplace,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: because even Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
did not disagree with him
except about a trash heap that is in the house,
but about a trash heap that is in the marketplace, he agrees with him,
and "appear correct," etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." means: and רבי חנינא's words appear correct to רבי יהודה in the house case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about how רבי could say each sage's words appear correct.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement: each sage agrees with the other in one specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי seemed to say two opposite opinions were both correct, which made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא agrees with רבי יהודה about the marketplace trash heap, and רבי יהודה agrees with רבי חנינא about the house.

steps.title: The משנה: a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are left out of slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: everyone may slaughter except a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן, because they might ruin the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor, because they might ruin their slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will learn something from its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said everyone may slaughter, and now it lists the exceptions: חרש, שוטה, and קטן. The reason it gives is that they might ruin the שחיטה. Keep the words 'שמא יקלקלו' in mind, because the next step depends on them.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, treated by הלכה as lacking full understanding
A minor, a child below the age of מצוות

phrases.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
lest they ruin their slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the found animals and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה, and קטן are excluded from slaughtering because they might ruin the שחיטה.

steps.title: Learning from the future tense: do not hand them animals to begin with
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'lest they ruin' (future), not 'lest they ruined' (past). From this, רבא learns that we do not give them חולין to slaughter לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה does not say 'lest they ruined,' but 'lest they will ruin.' רבא said: This shows that we do not hand them non-sacred animals to slaughter in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה uses the future tense. רבא learns a practical rule from this: we should not give these people animals to slaughter to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה were talking about a שחיטה that already happened, it would say 'lest they ruined.' Saying 'lest they will ruin' shows it is talking about the decision beforehand. So the משנה is telling us not to give them the animal in the first place, even though, as the next line will say, the שחיטה is kosher after the fact if others watched.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not teach (the wording the משנה chose not to use)
In the first place, before acting

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. לכתחילה we do not give them animals to slaughter, but בדיעבד, if they did slaughter while others watched, the שחיטה is כשרה (next step).

phrases.english: "Lest they ruined" is not what it teaches,
rather, "lest they will ruin."
Rava said: That is to say
we do not hand them non-sacred animals to slaughter in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the exact wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not give a חרש, שוטה, or קטן animals to slaughter לכתחילה.

steps.title: The משנה: if others watch them, their שחיטה is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if any of them slaughtered while others watched, the שחיטה is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them who slaughtered while others watched them, their slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, who cannot form proper intention, produces a kosher שחיטה if adults watched and saw it was done correctly. The watchers check that the cut was done properly. They do not supply any intention, so the problem of intention remains open for the next step.

phrases.english: And all of them who slaughtered
phrases.notes: "All of them" includes even the חרש, שוטה, and קטן just mentioned.

phrases.english: while others see them,
their slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the לכתחילה rule to what happens after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה, or קטן who slaughtered under supervision produces a valid שחיטה.

steps.title: Who holds that שחיטה needs no intention?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that no כוונה is needed for שחיטה, since these people cannot form proper intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that we do not need intention for slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sage's opinion the משנה follows, since it seems to say that intention is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, שוטה, and קטן have no intention that counts in הלכה. If their שחיטה still works, the משנה must hold that שחיטה works even without כוונה. The גמרא wants to know which sage holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage taught this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
who holds that we do not require intent for slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the idea hidden in step 4: that a שחיטה works without valid intention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that שחיטה does not require כוונה.

steps.title: It is רבי נתן, as shown by the case of the thrown knife
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי נתן. In a ברייתא, a knife thrown at a wall happened to slaughter an animal properly, and רבי נתן rules it כשר while חכמים rule it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is רבי נתן. אושעיא, the youngest of the group, taught: If someone threw a knife to stick it into the wall, and on the way it slaughtered an animal in the proper way, רבי נתן says it is valid and the חכמים say it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The משנה follows רבי נתן, who holds that a שחיטה done with no intention at all is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the knife case, nobody meant to slaughter. The person only meant to stick the knife into the wall. רבי נתן still accepts the שחיטה, so he clearly does not need כוונה, and that fits our משנה. The חכמים disagree and require intention.

keyTerms.meaning: To stick it into the wall

phrases.english: Rava said: It is Rabbi Natan,
as Oshaya, the youngest of the group, taught:
If one threw a knife to stick it into the wall,
and it went and slaughtered an animal in its proper way,
Rabbi Natan deems it valid,
and the Rabbis deem it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and brings a ברייתא as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי נתן, who accepts a שחיטה done with no intention, as in the thrown-knife case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא taught by אושעיא about a knife thrown at a wall.

steps.title: The one who taught the ברייתא rules like רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: אושעיא, who taught the ברייתא, also ruled that the הלכה follows רבי נתן: שחיטה does not need כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught it, and he said about it: The הלכה is like רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that the same אושעיא who taught the ברייתא also ruled הלכה כרבי נתן, so this is the practical law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step turns the dispute into a ruling. Since the הלכה follows רבי נתן, a שחיטה without intention is valid. That is why our משנה can accept the supervised שחיטה of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
He is the one who taught it (this ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: שחיטה does not require כוונה (הלכה כרבי נתן). Because of this, a חרש, שוטה, or קטן who slaughtered while others watched produces a valid שחיטה, but לכתחילה we do not give them animals to slaughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that the slaughterer's intention is not needed for a kosher שחיטה of חולין.

phrases.english: He teaches it,
phrases.notes: "He" is אושעיא, and "it" is the ברייתא about the thrown knife.

phrases.english: and he states about it:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Natan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute from step 6 in favor of רבי נתן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי נתן: שחיטה does not require intention.

steps.title: A thrown knife does not move back and forth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא of the thrown knife: a valid שחיטה needs the knife to go back and forth, and a thrown knife only moves one way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we require that the knife be moved back and forth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the case in the ברייתא from step 6, which רבי נתן ruled valid. How can a knife thrown at a wall make a valid שחיטה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper שחיטה needs the knife to go forward and come back across the neck. A knife thrown in the air flies in one direction only. So it seems it could never slaughter properly, with or without כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving forward and bringing back: the back-and-forth motion of the knife needed in שחיטה
But don't we require…? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But don't we require
moving back and forth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the case in רבי נתן's ברייתא is even possible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's case of a thrown knife that slaughtered properly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Valid שחיטה needs back-and-forth motion, and a thrown knife moves only one way.

steps.title: The knife went and came back in the normal way
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the knife hit the neck, bounced off the wall, and came back across the neck, so it did move back and forth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the knife went and came back in its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing the case more exactly. The knife went out and then came back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knife cut going toward the wall, bounced off it, and cut again on its way back. That gives the needed back-and-forth motion. So the ברייתא is about a real case, and the only question left is כוונה.

phrases.english: Where it went and came back in its normal way.
phrases.notes: The knife cut, bounced off the wall, and came back across the neck.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A thrown knife moves only one way, so it can never meet the back-and-forth requirement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The knife bounced back off the wall, so it did go back and forth.

steps.title: Does a child's thought count?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן asked whether a קטן has legally meaningful מחשבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן asked: Does a minor have legally meaningful thought, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבי יוחנן asks whether a child's thought or intention counts in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some הלכות depend only on what a person intends, even without doing anything. רבי יוחנן wants to know whether a קטן's intention can have that effect. This fits the topic just before it, about whether people without full understanding can do שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question he was unsure about
Thought or intention that has a legal effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said,
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
Does a minor have thought,
or does he not have thought?
phrases.notes: "Have thought" means thought that counts in הלכה, not whether the child can think.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the legal power of a קטן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קטן's intention alone has legal effect

steps.title: Why ask about thought if the משנה already answered it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי objects: no one asks about a child's action, because a משנה says they have מעשה. That same משנה says they lack מחשבה, so why ask?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: Then let him also ask about action! Why does he not ask about action? Because we learned, "They have action." Then he should not ask about thought either, because we learned, "They do not have thought."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי challenges רבי יוחנן's question. He says a משנה already answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי points out that nobody asks whether a child's action counts, since the משנה says it does. The same משנה also says children's thought does not count. So רבי יוחנן's question seems already settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him ask too (a sharp counter-question)
An action, a physical deed that has a legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מעשה and מחשבה. According to רבי אמי, the משנה says a child's actions count, but a child's thoughts alone do not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי חייא בר אבא, who reported the question.

phrases.english: Then let him also ask about action?
What is different about action
that he does not ask about it?
Because we learned: "They have action"?
phrases.notes: "They" are the חרש, the שוטה and the קטן.

phrases.english: Then about thought too he should not ask,
because we learned: "They do not have thought"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's question in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's question about a קטן's מחשבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה that settles מעשה also clearly settles מחשבה, so there is nothing left to ask.

steps.title: The משנה about shells that children hollowed out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the משנה: shells that children hollowed out for measuring dirt or for a scale become טמאין, because children have מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: An acorn, a pomegranate, or a nut that children hollowed out to measure dirt with, or that they set up as a pan for a scale, can become טמא, because they have action,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that רבי אמי relied on. The quote goes on into the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When children actually hollow out a shell to use it, their action turns it into a כלי, so it can become טמא. This is the "they have action" half of רבי אמי's proof. The "no thought" half comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: The pan of a balance scale
Able to become ritually impure, because they now count as כלים

phrases.english: As we learned: An acorn, a pomegranate, or a nut
that children hollowed out
to measure dirt with them,
or that they set up as a pan for a scale –
they can become impure,
because they have action,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual text of the משנה that רבי אמי cited in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That children have legally effective מעשה but not מחשבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about hollowed shells used for measuring or as a scale pan
